summary: Bo Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University, attested in 2008, under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.
Bo-gwang Han is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Dongguk University, attested in 2004 and 2015. He also taught Silwon Suk.

Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kalu Rinpoche from circa 1960 to 1989 and held a post at Bokar Ngedon Choekhor Ling Monastery from circa 1984 to 2004.

Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser, also studying under Jacqueline I. Stone and Lewis Lancaster.

Bongkil Chung works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and held posts at Florida International University from 1991 to 1992 and as professor of philosophy in 2012.

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky circa 1920–1925 and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Brad Warner (born 1964) is active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Wadsworth High School and Kent State University, and received training under Tim McCarthy (~1983–1993) and Gudo Wafu Nishijima (attested 2017).

Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned degrees from the University of Virginia (BA 1989; PhD 2004 under David Germano) and Harvard University (MTS 1993), also studying at Naropa University.
Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal (1921–2022) studied at the University of Allahabad and worked in Indology and archaeology. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson (born 1978) is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and held posts at SOAS (~2006–2009) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2010–2018).
Brandon J. Harwood is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015) under the supervision of Patrick Pranke.

Brendan S. Gillon works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1976–1985) and became an Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University circa 1992.

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Vanderbilt and Kyoto University, held research and teaching posts in Japan, and taught philosophy at Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).
Brian Bocking works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.

Brian D. Ruppert (born 1962), a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies mentored by Willis Stoesz, held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) before joining Bates College circa 2018.

Brian Daizen Victoria (born 1939) works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. Educated at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple universities, he later held posts at Antioch University (attested 2010) and the University of Adelaide (attested 2011).

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University in 2005 under the doctoral supervision of György Kara.

Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar educated at East India Company College, Haileybury, and Fort William College. He served as Assistant Resident (1820) and British Resident in Nepal (~1833–1843).

Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned his PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under doctoral supervisor Anne Carolyn Klein.
